import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 599

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/599](https://www.erdosproblems.com/599)
- [AhBe09] Aharoni, Ron and Berger, Eli, *Menger's theorem for infinite graphs*,
  *Invent. Math.* **176** (2009), 1--62.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos599

/--
**Erdős Problem 599** (the Erdős–Menger conjecture).

Let $G$ be a (possibly infinite) graph and let $A, B$ be disjoint independent sets of
vertices. Must there exist a family $P$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint paths from $A$ to $B$,
and a set $S$ of vertices containing exactly one vertex from each path in $P$, such that
every path from $A$ to $B$ contains at least one vertex of $S$?

For finite $G$ this is equivalent to Menger's theorem. The answer is **yes**, proved by
Aharoni and Berger [AhBe09].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      Disjoint A B → G.IsIndepSet A → G.IsIndepSet B →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  sorry

/--
**Menger's theorem for infinite graphs** (Aharoni–Berger [AhBe09]).

The theorem actually proved by Aharoni and Berger holds for arbitrary vertex sets $A$
and $B$: in any (possibly infinite) graph $G$ there is a family $P$ of pairwise
vertex-disjoint $A$--$B$ paths together with an $A$--$B$ separator $S$ consisting of the
choice of exactly one vertex from each path in $P$. The disjointness and independence
hypotheses of `erdos_599` are not needed.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: when $A = \varnothing$ the conclusion of `erdos_599` holds trivially, with
the empty family of paths and $S = \varnothing$ (the covering condition is vacuous since
there is no path starting in $\varnothing$).
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599.test.empty_A (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (B : Set V) :
    ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
      (∀ i, a i ∈ (∅ : Set V)) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
      (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
      S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
      (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
      (∀ a' ∈ (∅ : Set V), ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath →
        ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  refine ⟨Empty, Empty.elim, Empty.elim, fun i => i.elim, ∅,
    fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim,
    fun v hv => hv.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun a' ha' => absurd ha' (Set.notMem_empty _)⟩

end Erdos599

reformulations.difference: The source describes S as consisting of a choice of precisely one vertex from each path. Lean instead requires S to be contained in the union of the path supports and to intersect each support in exactly one vertex.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For pairwise disjoint supports Tᵢ, these conditions are equivalent to the existence of f : ι → V with f i ∈ Tᵢ and S = Set.range f. In one direction, choose the unique intersection points; the subset condition excludes extra elements of S. Conversely, disjointness prevents a point selected from another path from lying on Tᵢ. The equivalence for the entire existential conclusion was proved as certificate_iff_choice in /workspace/review/certificates.lean, without using either sorry theorem.

reformulations.difference: As in the main declaration, the source's choice-of-one-vertex formulation is expressed through a subset-of-union condition and unique intersections, rather than an explicit selection function.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same certificate_iff_choice proof applies to arbitrary A and B: it assumes neither disjointness nor independence of the endpoint sets. Pairwise disjointness of the path supports makes the two descriptions of S equivalent.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/599 (read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/599 after direct requests returned a browser challenge)
Aharoni and Berger, Menger's theorem for infinite graphs, arXiv:math/0509397v4: Theorem 1.6, Definition 1.3, and §2.3 (LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0509397v4)
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The affirmative answer and both research-solved tags agree with the sources. The Aharoni–Berger variant is the undirected specialization of their theorem for arbitrary vertex sets in digraphs. The paper explicitly defines A–B paths as finite and permits singleton paths, matching Walk with IsPath. Lean checks covered empty endpoint sets, edgeless graphs, A = B (including infinite sets), and a single-edge example. They also verified that the separator contains A ∩ B and that an empty family cannot satisfy the conclusion when an A–B path exists. Both scratch files compiled without errors; the file's empty_A proof has no sorry dependency. The reviewed file remains unchanged.
